title: How do you build a training matrix for a childcare service?
description: Build a childcare training matrix: qualifications, child safety, first aid, screening and food safety by role, with renewal clocks and inspection records.
shortAnswer: A childcare training matrix is built by listing each role in the service, from approved provider and nominated supervisor to educators, cooks, volunteers and students on placement, against the qualification, child safety, first aid, screening and food safety obligations that apply where the service operates. Each cell records the clock (many are fixed, such as annual CPR), the trigger, and the certificate or register entry an authorized officer will ask to see.
keyTakeaways: Childcare differs from most sectors because many clocks are fixed in law or regulator guidance: CPR every year, first aid every three years, child safety refreshers every two years.
Keep three registers side by side: qualifications and training, screening clearances, and certificates such as first aid and food safety supervisor. A check is not training.
Role matters more than job title: nominated supervisors and persons in day-to-day charge carry extra child protection duties, and volunteers and students are in scope for child safety training.
Inspectors check certificates, registers and staff records, so every cell needs an evidence rule, not just a completion flag.
As at November 2026, transitional educator provisions end on 31 December 2026 and advanced child safety training is due by 31 March 2027 for existing role holders.

sections.heading: Why is a childcare training matrix different from other sectors?

blocks.text: A childcare matrix tracks expiry dates more than learning hours, because the rules that govern early childhood services attach to certificates that lapse and to clearances that can be withdrawn. A service can be out of compliance overnight if one educator's CPR currency runs out on a day when that person is the only first aider rostered.

The library's regulation pages for this sector are Australian, so this guide uses Australia as the worked example. Services in other countries can follow the same structure and substitute their own regulator's rules. The general method in [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) applies; what childcare adds is roster awareness, since ratios, first aid cover and supervisor availability are tested shift by shift, and a strong separation between screening and training.

sections.heading: Which childcare roles need separate rows?

blocks.text: Create a row wherever the law assigns a distinct duty, and include people who are not employees. In Australian services that covers leadership roles, educator qualification levels, family day care roles, support staff, and volunteers and students.

sections.heading: Which obligations fill the columns of a childcare matrix?

blocks.text: Five families of obligation fill the columns: qualifications, child safety and protection, screening, first aid, and food safety, with general employment duties such as harassment prevention alongside. The summaries below come from the linked regulation pages.

items: **Qualifications.** Regulation 126 of the Education and Care Services National Regulations requires at least 50% of educators counted in ratios at a center-based service for children preschool age or under to hold, or be actively working towards, an approved diploma, and the rest an approved certificate III. Only qualifications on the list kept by the Australian Children's Education and Care Quality Authority (ACECQA), or assessed as equivalent, count ([NQF educator qualifications](/regulations/national-quality-framework-educator-qualifications)).

**Child safety training.** Since 27 February 2026, national child safety training is mandatory for everyone working or volunteering in NQF services: foundation courses within 14 days or before working directly with children, and refreshers every two years. In NSW, nominated supervisors, persons in day-to-day charge and family day care co-ordinators must also complete an approved child protection course under section 162A, and in-house training is not sufficient ([NSW early childhood child protection](/regulations/child-protection-training-early-childhood-nsw)).

**Child Safe Standards.** NSW services must implement the 10 NSW Child Safe Standards, where Standard 7 covers continual education and training. In Victoria, Standard 8 of the 11 Child Safe Standards requires ongoing education and training, beginning with training to implement the Child Safety and Wellbeing Policy (requirement 8.1) ([Victoria Child Safe Standards](/regulations/victoria-child-safe-standards-training)).

**Reporting duties.** From 24 April 2026, NSW changes to regulation 84 require staff to understand child protection law and be able to explain their mandatory reporting obligations and how to make a report. Reporting thresholds and channels are set by state law and differ between states ([mandatory reporting](/regulations/mandatory-reporting-training-australia)).

**Screening.** A Working with Children Check is a clearance, not training. NSW employers must verify each worker online and record seven details; Victorian organizations may engage only a person with a clearance, a pending application or an exemption; Queensland requires a blue card linked before the worker starts ([Working with Children Checks](/regulations/working-with-children-check-requirements)).

**First aid.** Regulation 136 requires current approved first aid, anaphylaxis management and emergency asthma management training. Under the general workplace rules, the model WHS Regulation 42 requires an adequate number of trained first aiders ([workplace first aid](/regulations/first-aid-training-requirements-australia)).

**Food safety.** The NSW Food Authority lists children's services providing meals among the businesses that must appoint a food safety supervisor per premises, with a certificate renewed every five years ([NSW food safety supervisor](/regulations/nsw-food-safety-supervisor-requirements)). Nationally, Standard 3.2.2A requires food handlers in category one and two businesses to complete a food safety training course before handling ([Standard 3.2.2A](/regulations/food-safety-standard-3-2-2a-training)); services should confirm their category with their food regulator.

**Harassment prevention.** Section 47C of the Sex Discrimination Act 1984 applies to employers of any size, and the Australian Human Rights Commission expects ongoing, role tailored education rather than one off induction ([positive duty](/regulations/positive-duty-sexual-harassment-training)).

sections.heading: Which childcare renewal clocks are fixed and which are left to the provider?

blocks.text: More childcare clocks are fixed than in most sectors, but several important ones are still left to the provider. Record each clock exactly as the source states it, and note where the service has chosen its own.

items: **Fixed by regulation or regulator.** From 1 October 2023, first aid, anaphylaxis and emergency asthma training are current if completed in the previous three years, and CPR and emergency life support in the previous year. National child safety refreshers are due every two years. NSW food safety supervisor certificates expire five years from issue, and a business has 30 days to recertify or appoint another supervisor.

**Recommended, not required.** Section 162A does not require refresher training, but the NSW Early Learning Commission recommends refreshers every 12 to 24 months. The model first aid Code of Practice recommends annual CPR refreshers and three year requalification for workplaces generally. FSANZ sets no refresher period for food handler training and calls regular refreshers best practice.

**Left to the service.** Victoria's compliance indicators expect policy training at induction and at regular intervals without fixing the interval. The positive duty guidance says one off induction training has proven ineffective unless periodically reinforced.

**Triggers that restart a row.** A move into a nominated supervisor or day-to-day charge role, a change of service location across state lines, an expired clearance, or a policy change should each open new rows. See [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

sections.heading: What records will an authorized officer ask a childcare service for?

blocks.text: Expect to produce certificates, registers and staff records on the day of a visit, not a summary report. Authorized officers may check certificates and the National Early Childhood Worker Register.

items: **Child safe environment policy records.** From 24 April 2026, NSW regulation 168(2)(h) requires child safe environment policies to cover child protection training with up-to-date records, and regulation 151 requires the Working with Children Check number in educator records. Staff records sit under regulations 153 and 177.
**Training register.** Victoria's compliance indicators expect a training action plan, a training register and leaders telling staff and volunteers that child safety training is mandatory.

**Screening registers.** NSW employers record full name, date of birth, check number, verification date, outcome, expiry and paid or volunteer status. Queensland organizations must keep an employee register, with a maximum penalty of 50 penalty units for failing to.
**Certificates on site.** A copy of the NSW food safety supervisor certificate must be kept on the premises, and only approved first aid training satisfies regulation 136.

**Enforcement exposure.** Failing to have a worker hold a Queensland blue card and be linked before starting carries up to 200 penalty units ($34,540) or two years in prison. In Victoria, failing to comply with a Social Services Regulator improvement notice carries up to 1,200 penalty units for a body corporate. The guide on [preparing training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) covers record design.

sections.heading: Which childcare deadlines fall in late 2026 and 2027?

blocks.text: Two deadlines fall within the next five months, so they should already be in the matrix as dated rows. As at November 2026, the regulation pages record these changes:

items: **31 December 2026:** regulation 242 (taken to be an early childhood teacher while studying) and the regulation 239A remote area provisions are scheduled to expire in the states and territories where they still apply. Rows that rely on them need a replacement plan.
**31 March 2027:** advanced child safety training is due for people who were already in relevant roles before 30 September 2026.

**Already in effect in 2026:** national child safety training became mandatory on 27 February 2026, responsibility for Victoria's Child Safe Standards moved to the Social Services Regulator in February 2026, and NSW regulation 84 and 168 changes took effect on 24 April 2026. Check that induction content reflects all three.

blocks.title: Screening rules are moving too
blocks.text: Victoria's July 2026 reforms allow child safety risk information to be considered in Working with Children Check assessments, and the NSW Office of the Children's Guardian compliance and enforcement policy is under review in 2026. Keep the screening register owner on both watch lists.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records each childcare obligation with its source, the role it attaches to, its currency period and the evidence that satisfies it, so an expiring certificate or a changed regulation flags the affected educators before a roster gap appears. See [compliance programs](/programs/compliance).

faqs.q: Does a Working with Children Check count as child protection training?
faqs.a: No. A check is a screening clearance showing a person has been cleared, not that they have been trained in child safety, reporting or the service's code of conduct. Keep screening in its own register alongside the training matrix and link the two by person.

faqs.q: Do volunteers and students on placement need child safety training?
faqs.a: Yes. National child safety training applies to everyone working or volunteering in NQF services, and NSW lists regular volunteers and students on placement for an approved early childhood qualification among those in scope. Give them their own rows so their deadlines are tracked.

faqs.q: Can a service deliver its own child protection course for nominated supervisors?
faqs.a: Not in NSW. Section 162A training for nominated supervisors, persons in day-to-day charge and family day care co-ordinators means an approved course such as CHCPRT025 or CHCPRT026, and the NSW Early Learning Commission says in-house training is not sufficient.

faqs.q: How many first aid trained educators does a service need?
faqs.a: Regulation 136 sets the requirement for education and care services, and only approved first aid, anaphylaxis and asthma training counts. Build the roster so that the required cover is present at all times, and record CPR currency separately because it lasts one year rather than three.
